We have search results with many templates. Need to find one that when applied to the given molecule reproduces the reaction (retro step). The initial molecule is given with atom mapping: [CH2:1]=[C:2]([c:3]1[cH:4][cH:5][cH:6][cH:7][cH:8]1)[C@@H:9]1[CH2:10][CH2:11][CH2:12][C@@:13]1([OH:14])[C:15]([F:16])([F:17])[F:18]

We need to return mapped_rxn and template_id (integer). The search returned templates with reaction_id and template_hash etc. The template_id likely is reaction_id? The description says "template_id (the one used to search the database not the hash) as an integer". So use reaction_id.

We need to find which template matches our molecule and corresponds to carbonyl-ene reaction (intramolecular). Look at results: reaction_id 4147 etc. Let's examine each.

First entry reaction_id 4147: retro_smarts_template: '[C:1]-[CH;D3;+0:2](-[OH;D1;+0:3])-[C:4]-[C:5]=[C:6]>>[C:1]-[C;H0;D3;+0:2](=[O;H0;D1;+0:3])-[C:4]-[C:5]=[C:6]'

This seems like conversion of allylic alcohol to carbonyl (reverse of ene). The forward reaction would be carbonyl-ene: carbonyl + alkene -> allylic alcohol. The retro would break C-O bond to form carbonyl. This matches.

Our molecule has an allylic alcohol? The structure: CH2= C( aromatic ) - chiral carbon attached to cyclobutane? Actually we have a cyclobutane? Let's decode: [CH2:1]=[C:2]([c:3]1... ) [C@@H:9]1[CH2:10][CH2:11][CH2:12][C@@:13]1([OH:14])[C:15]([F:16])([F:17])[F:18]

So there is an alkene (CH2= C) attached to aromatic ring and to a cyclobutane bearing OH and CF3. This looks like product of carbonyl-ene where carbonyl turned into OH after reaction? Actually carbonyl-ene forms new C-C bond and OH at allylic position. So product has OH attached to carbon that was originally carbonyl carbon? In our molecule OH is on a carbon in cyclobutane (C@@:13) attached to CF3. The carbonyl would have been at that carbon originally? The retro would break C-O bond to form carbonyl (C=O) and generate alkene? The template 4147 seems to convert an allylic alcohol to carbonyl (C=O) while preserving alkene.

Thus likely template 4147 matches.

We need to verify if template matches our molecule. Use check_smiles_reaction_template_matching with template_id? The tool expects template_id (string). We have reaction_id? Not sure. The search result includes template_hash and retro_smarts_template. The template_id likely is the reaction_id? The tool check expects template_id string referencing template catalog. Might accept reaction_id as string? Not sure. Could try with "4147". Let's test.
